title: Quieting and hardening SLO pager signals after capacity regression
creator: Liam Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity regression on 2026-03-08 we observed an SLO breach for 99th-percentile generation latency across two regional pools. The immediate consequence was a burst of burn-rate alerts that paged multiple on-call rotations, causing noise and delayed triage of the root issue. Root-cause analysis points to an orchestration scheduler change plus a cache eviction policy regression that increased tail latency under load. This ticket collects postmortem action items aimed specifically at reducing paging noise from burn-rate and SLO alerts, hardening thresholds, and improving signal correlation so that only actionable incidents page engineers. Work spans runtime config, alerting rules, runbooks, and oncall tooling.
action_items: Add a 5-minute sustained-window requirement to burn-rate pager rule (only page if burn > 1.5x target for 5 continuous minutes)
Introduce correlated-signal requirement: burn-rate alert must be accompanied by either >3% 5xx rate or sustained p50/p95 latency increase before paging
Create tiered burn-rate thresholds by customer tier and region (prod-high, prod-medium, prod-low) and map to escalation levels rather than immediate paging
Implement cooldown suppression for duplicate burn alerts per resource (10 minute suppression after page) and add dedup key by pool-id
Tune KV cache eviction parameters and test with synthetic load to verify tail latency regression is resolved (runtime change tracked separately)
Add a Grafana dashboard tile and Alertmanager group for correlated burn+error signals and expose to oncall with runbook links
Update the oncall runbook: triage checklist, quick mitigation knobs (route to fallback model, increase pool capacity, disable new scheduler), and post-page owner assignment rules
Ship a small client library change in metrics ingestion to emit stable 'pool_id' tags so alerts deduplicate correctly (PR linked below)
